_note: CoffeeBot knowledge base. A topic fires when EVERY 'when' group matches at least one phrase. Public facts only: never the backend IP, panel, database or how auth works. Placeholders: {address} {discord} {wiki} {status} {online} {max} {tps} {tpsVerdict} {uptimeDays} {session} {me.*}. Server-side additions/overrides: config/coffeebot-kb.json, then /aerobot reload.

topics.title: Hi, I'm CoffeeBot ☕
topics.answer:
I'm the server's help desk. Ask me anything, for example:
• how do I join?
• is the server up?
• how do I craft andesite alloy?
• is <player> online?
• what's my level?
• my game crashes while loading
Right now: **{online}/{max}** online at **{tps} TPS**. I answer from the wiki, the server's live data and what staff have taught me.

topics.title: Anytime ☕
topics.answer: Happy to help. If anything else comes up, just mention me.

topics.title: All good up here
topics.answer: Running at **{tps} TPS** ({tpsVerdict}) with **{online}/{max}** pilots aboard. What can I help you with?

topics.title: What I can do
topics.answer:
I'm a rule-based expert system, not a chatbot that makes things up. I can:
• answer questions about joining, installing, crashes, accounts, claims, ships, rewards, rules and more
• look things up live: who's online, when someone was last seen, how to craft any item, what a mod is, when the next restart is
• walk you through problems one question at a time
• tell you *why* I answered what I did (say `why`)
If I don't know something I say so, and staff teach me.
Thank you. Brewed fresh every restart.

topics.title: Fair enough
topics.answer: If I got something wrong, tell me what you were trying to find out and I'll do better. Staff see the questions I miss and teach me the answers.

topics.title: How to join
topics.answer:
Join with **`{address}`** (no port needed), or press the **Join** button on the pack's main menu.
You need the modpack first: {wiki}/getting-started

topics.title: Installing the pack
topics.answer:
Install **Coffee's Create: Aeronautics SMP** from Modrinth (Modrinth App, Prism, ATLauncher or any launcher that takes an `.mrpack`).
On the very first launch it downloads a few mods Modrinth can't host, so: launch, wait for the title screen, close it, launch again.
Using CurseForge? Grab the CurseForge zip from our Discord and import it.

topics.title: CurseForge
topics.answer: The Season 3 CurseForge listing is waiting on CurseForge's review. Until then, get the CurseForge zip from our Discord and import it: CurseForge app, *Create Custom Profile*, *Import*, pick the zip. It keeps itself up to date just like the Modrinth version.

topics.title: First launch
topics.answer: On Modrinth the first launch downloads FTB and the mods that depend on it. Let it reach the title screen, **close the game, then launch it again**. After that it behaves normally.

topics.title: Pack version and updates
topics.answer:
The pack updates itself from the title screen: when a new version is out you get a prompt, accept it and restart the game.
If the server says your mods don't match, update first. Full notes are on the News screen in game.

topics.title: Can't join
topics.answer:
Work through these in order:
1. Is the server up? Right now it's **{status}** ({online}/{max} online).
2. Use **`{address}`**, or the Join button on the pack's main menu.
3. Make sure the pack is up to date (the title screen prompts you).
4. RAM: **8 GB** is the sweet spot.
Still failing? Pick what you see below and I'll narrow it down.
topics.ask: What do you see when it fails?

options.label: The game crashes before I even get there

topics.title: "Hash mismatch after download"
topics.answer:
That's the in-game updater catching a half-fresh download right after we publish an update. GitHub's servers can serve old files for about **5 minutes** after a release.
Wait five minutes, then restart the game and accept the update again. It fixes itself.

topics.title: Mod or version mismatch
topics.answer:
Your pack doesn't match the server's. Restart the game and accept the update on the title screen.
If you added or removed mods by hand, undo that, since the updater manages the `mods` folder. If it still won't match, reinstall the pack from Modrinth (or the CurseForge zip from Discord).

topics.title: Timed out / can't reach the server
topics.answer:
Right now the server is **{status}** ({online}/{max} online).
If it's up: double check the address is **`{address}`** with no port, try once more (the first join after a restart is slow), and if you're on a VPN or school/work network, try without it.
If it's down it's almost always a restart or maintenance. Watch the announcements here.

topics.title: Whitelist
topics.answer: The whitelist only goes on for testing or maintenance. If you're seeing it, the server is mid-maintenance. Check announcements here and try again shortly.

topics.title: Is the server up?
topics.answer:
The server is **{status}**: {online}/{max} pilots online, running at **{tps} TPS** ({tpsVerdict}).
Live status page: {wiki}/status

topics.title: Who's online
topics.answer: **{online}/{max}** pilots online right now.

topics.title: Restarts
topics.answer: The server restarts daily at **10:30 IST**, with a 10-minute warning in game, plus short restarts for updates. Restarts are announced here. Current session: up for {session}.

topics.title: Uptime
topics.answer: Coffee's Aero SMP has been flying for **{uptimeDays} days**. This session has been up for {session}. The `/uptime` slash command shows the same.

topics.title: Lag and ping
topics.answer:
Right now the server is at **{tps} TPS** ({tpsVerdict}).
If TPS is near 20, what you feel is your connection or your FPS, not the server. Your ping can read high for the first minutes after joining while map data and distant terrain stream in, then it settles.
If the server itself is struggling, staff can see it too and are on it.
topics.ask: What kind of lag is it?

options.label: Low FPS, my game is choppy

topics.title: Low FPS
topics.answer:
In this order:
1. RAM: **8 GB**
2. Shaders off, or a lower preset
3. Render distance 8 to 12 and let Distant Horizons draw the horizon
4. **Potato mode**: the Mode button in Aero Settings (the gear tile on the main menu). It switches off the heaviest client extras and can be flipped back anytime
5. Close the browser and other heavy apps
topics.ask: Want details on one of these?

options.label: How much RAM to give it

topics.title: How much RAM
topics.answer:
**8 GB** for most people.
- Under 6 GB: runs out of memory and stutters
- 10 to 12 GB: fine **only if your PC has 32 GB or more**
- More than about half your PC's RAM: the game dies while loading with **no crash report**, because your graphics driver and Distant Horizons need memory outside Minecraft's share

topics.title: Game closes with no crash report
topics.answer:
That's almost always **too much RAM**, not too little. Minecraft's allocation is only part of what the game uses; give it so much that nothing is left for your graphics driver and Distant Horizons, and it dies mid-load with no report.
Lower the allocation by 2 GB and try again. **8 GB** is the sweet spot.

topics.title: Crashes
topics.answer:
Two quick checks first:
1. RAM: **8 GB**. More than half your PC's memory crashes the game without a report.
2. Shaders off, if you turned them on.
Still crashing? Post the crash report (in `crash-reports` inside your instance folder) in our Discord, or open a ticket in game with `/ticket <what happened>`.

options.label: While loading, with no crash report
It doesn't crash, it's just slow

topics.title: macOS
topics.answer: On a Mac: use the default Java garbage collector (G1), **not ZGC**, keep `-XstartOnFirstThread` in the JVM arguments, and give it 4 to 8 GB depending on your Mac's memory.

topics.title: Do I need to buy Minecraft?
topics.answer:
No. The server is **hybrid**: premium and offline (non-premium) accounts both join at **`{address}`** and get the same features, custom skins included.
Offline players register a password on first join (`/register <password> <password>`, typed twice) and use `/login <password>` after that.

topics.title: Register and log in
topics.answer:
Offline accounts: `/register <password> <password>` on your first join (the same password twice), then `/login <password>` every time after. You have **3 minutes** to log in before you're kicked; just reconnect if that happens.
Premium accounts are verified automatically and never need a password.

topics.title: Forgot or change password
topics.answer:
Know your old password? Change it in game with `/changepassword <old> <new>`.
Forgot it? Ask staff in Discord to reset it; they'll check it's really your account first.
Staff will **never** ask you for your password. Anyone who does is not staff.

topics.title: Kicked at login
topics.answer: You get **3 minutes** after joining to `/login <password>` (offline accounts). Past that you're kicked; reconnect and log in straight away.

topics.title: AFK
topics.answer:
Idle for **10 minutes** and you're marked AFK: that time stops counting toward playtime and level, and you're sent back to the lobby. Press Join to carry on.
AFK machines and auto-clickers to dodge it count as cheating.

topics.title: The lobby
topics.answer: Everyone arrives in the lobby first; from there you're sent on to the survival world. If you were sent back mid-game, it was the AFK timer (10 minutes idle). Press Join to go back in.

topics.title: Skins and capes
topics.answer: Use `/skin <name>` in game to wear any Minecraft player's skin. **Offline players can use it too.**

topics.title: Commands
topics.answer:
**Getting around:** `/spawn`, `/home` (to your bed, 5 min cooldown), `/rtp` (random wilderness, 15 min), `/back` (after a death or teleport, 3 min)
**Rewards:** `/mail`, `/daily`, `/vote`
**Ships:** `/shipname <name>`
**Account:** `/register`, `/login`, `/changepassword`, `/skin <name>`, `/discord link`
**Help:** `/ticket <message>`
`/tpa` and warps are off for Season 3. Full list: {wiki}/commands

topics.title: Teleporting
topics.answer:
Season 3 keeps teleporting to a minimum. You can use `/spawn`, `/home` (to your bed), `/rtp` (random wilderness) and `/back`.
`/tpa` and warps are **off**, so you can't teleport to other players. Build a railway or an airship.

topics.title: /rtp
topics.answer:
`/rtp` drops you **1,500 to 10,000 blocks** out into the Overworld wilderness, every **15 minutes**.
**Stand perfectly still** until you arrive: the server is preparing your destination, and moving cancels it. A cancelled teleport doesn't use up your cooldown. Doesn't work while combat-tagged.

topics.title: /home
topics.answer: `/home` takes you to your **bed / respawn point**, with a 5-minute cooldown. There's no separate sethome: sleep in a bed (or set your spawn) where you want home to be.

topics.title: /spawn
topics.answer: `/spawn` takes you back to world spawn. It doesn't work while you're combat-tagged.

topics.title: /back
topics.answer: `/back` returns you to where you died or last teleported from (within 5 minutes). It has a **3-minute** cooldown and a **5-second** countdown. You arrive as a ghost for up to 60 seconds: nothing can hurt you and mobs ignore you until you interact with something other than your corpse. It doesn't work while combat-tagged.

topics.title: When you die
topics.answer:
Your items stay in a **corpse** where you died, so you can go back for them. `/back` takes you there (3-minute cooldown, and you arrive as a ghost so you can grab your things safely).
Disconnecting during a fight is different: see combat logging.

topics.title: Combat logging
topics.answer: Hit or get hit by a player and you're combat-tagged for **30 seconds**. Disconnect while tagged and you **die**, dropping your items where the fight was. It's automatic. `/spawn`, `/home`, `/rtp` and `/back` are blocked while tagged.

topics.title: PvP
topics.answer: PvP is **on**. If you don't want a fight, don't start one and don't linger where one is happening. Spawn-camping and hunting the same new player is harassment.

topics.title: Land claims
topics.answer:
Open the map with **M** and click chunks to claim them.
You start with **5 chunks** and get **2 more every level**, up to **150**. Claims are full-height columns from bedrock to sky.
Ships need their own claim, separate from land (see ship claims). Read before you build: {wiki}/claims

topics.title: Can't break or place blocks
topics.answer:
Almost always a claim:
1. Are you inside someone else's claim? Press **M**. Claims are full-height, so check even while flying high above them
2. Is the ship claimed by someone else? Ship claims are separate from land
3. Did you pick your ship up and re-place it after claiming? That orphans the claim; claim it again

options.label: I'm on or above someone else's land
I picked my ship up and put it back down

topics.title: Teams and sharing claims
topics.answer: Form a party so friends can build with you. **Everyone brings their own allowance**: each member's chunks add to the team's pool, and everything the team claims works for everyone in it. If someone leaves, the pool shrinks with them.

topics.title: Claiming a ship
topics.answer:
Place a **claim block** on the ship. Each claim covers **250 ship blocks** and spends one chunk from your land allowance.
The order that matters: **place, then claim, then name**. Never pick a claimed ship up with a portable structure item: re-placing it gives it a new ID and orphans the claim.

options.label: Controls stop working over someone's land

topics.title: Ship lost its claim
topics.answer:
A ship claim is bound to the ship's internal ID. Picking the ship up with a portable structure item and placing it again creates a **new ID**, so the old claim no longer protects it and is wasted.
Claim it again with a claim block, and stop capturing it after that.

topics.title: Naming a ship
topics.answer: Stand on the ship and run `/shipname <name>`. `/shipname info` shows the current name, `/shipname clear` removes it. Only the owner can rename a claimed ship.

topics.title: Can't use my ship over someone's land
topics.answer: Land claims are full-height columns. Flying over someone's claimed chunk puts you inside **their** claim at any altitude, and you can't interact with your own ship there. Move off their land and try again.

topics.title: Airships
topics.answer:
Create: Aeronautics is why the server exists. Build your ship on the ground as a normal structure, then assemble it and it flies with real physics. Drive-By-Wire lets you steer from the cockpit.
Test small first, claim before you fly off, and name it right after claiming. Guide: {wiki}/airships

topics.title: Create: machine stopped
topics.answer: When a Create machine stops for no obvious reason it's almost always **stress**: you're asking for more work than your generators supply. Add another generator, or slow things down. Wear **Goggles** and look at any Create block to see its speed and stress.

topics.title: New to Create
topics.answer:
Create runs on rotation. Something spins, shafts and cogs carry it, machines use it. Start with **Andesite Alloy** (zinc and iron), a **Water Wheel** for power, then a Millstone or Mechanical Press. Wear **Goggles** to see speed and stress on any block.
Shortest path to your first airship: {wiki}/create-basics

topics.title: Mail and the starter kit
topics.answer: Everything the server gives you arrives as **mail**: the starter kit (300 spurs, bread and saplings), level rewards, `/daily` and votes. Type `/mail` and claim the attachments. Unclaimed mail expires after **60 days**.

topics.title: /daily
topics.answer: `/daily` every **20 hours**, in the Overworld. It runs a 7-day cycle of items plus XP; the XP lands right away and the items arrive in `/mail`. Leave it longer than 40 hours and the streak resets.

topics.title: Voting
topics.answer: Run `/vote` in game for the link. Voting pays spurs and diamonds by mail, even if you're offline, and grows with your streak: **2 to 10 spurs** and **1 to 5 diamonds**. Once every 24 hours; miss 48 and the streak restarts. Your first 30 votes are rewarded.

topics.title: Money (spurs)
topics.answer: The currency is **spurs** from Create: Numismatics, real items you can put on a belt. The server only pays spurs through the starter kit and voting; the rest is the player economy: sell to players and build shops (most trade gets arranged here in Discord). Coins drop when you die, so don't carry your savings into a fight.

topics.title: How levels work
topics.answer: Your level comes from **advancements** (10 XP each) and **Season 3 playtime** (6 XP per hour): `Level = 1 + √(XP ÷ 5)`. Every level adds **2 claim chunks** (up to 150) and mails you a reward; every 5th level is a milestone with 4 diamonds and 16 bottles o' enchanting. AFK time doesn't count.

topics.title: Your stats
topics.answer:
**{me.name}**: {me.seasonHours} h this season, {me.totalHours} h all time.
{me.levelLine}
topics.unlinked: I don't know who you are in game yet. Link your account: run `/discord link` in game, then `/link <code>` here in Discord. After that, ask me again.

topics.title: Leaderboard
topics.answer: Use the `/leaderboard` slash command here in Discord: top 10 by playtime this season (there's an all-time board too). Link your account (`/discord link` in game, then `/link <code>` here) to appear on it.

topics.title: Linking Discord
topics.answer: In game, run `/discord link` to get a code. Then here in Discord run `/link <code>`. Linked players show their server identity in chat and appear on `/leaderboard`.

topics.title: The Nether and the End
topics.answer: The **Nether is open**. The **End is closed** for now; when it opens it'll be announced here, and the dragon's island can never be claimed.

topics.title: Seasons and resets
topics.answer: We're in **Season 3**. A new season resets the world so everyone starts fresh together. Your account, password, skin and lifetime playtime carry over; builds, items, claims and level don't. Season endings are announced here well ahead.

topics.title: Rules
topics.answer:
Short version: don't take or break other people's stuff, don't cheat, don't be a nuisance. English in main chat, no slurs, harassment or advertising, one account per person for claims. Full rules: {wiki}/rules
Think a decision was wrong? Appeal here in Discord, not in game chat.

topics.title: Alt accounts
topics.answer: One account per person for claim purposes: using alts to multiply your chunk allowance isn't allowed. Sharing an account is at your own risk.

topics.title: Adding your own mods
topics.answer:
Client-side visual mods are usually fine (minimaps, shaders, sound mods). Anything that gives an unfair advantage, like x-ray, radars or cheat clients, gets you removed.
The updater manages the `mods` folder and removes older duplicates of pack mods, so only add things the pack doesn't already ship. Unsure? Ask staff first.

topics.title: Shaders
topics.answer: Shaders ship **off** and are the most expensive thing you can turn on. Start from a low preset and work up: compiling a heavy pack needs extra memory outside the game's allocation at the same moment Distant Horizons wants it.

topics.title: Distant Horizons
topics.answer: Distant Horizons draws terrain far past your render distance, which is most of the point of flying. Struggling? **Lower your render distance before turning DH off**: vanilla chunks cost far more than DH's simplified terrain. Potato mode in Aero Settings switches it off for you.

topics.title: Voice chat
topics.answer: The pack includes **Simple Voice Chat** (proximity voice). Press **V** in game to open its menu and pick your mic. By default you talk with push-to-talk on **Caps Lock**. Groups let you talk to friends anywhere.

topics.title: Getting help from staff
topics.answer:
In game: `/ticket <what happened>` (up to 2 a day) sends it straight to staff with your location. Staff reply by mail; `/ticket list` shows yours.
Or ask here in Discord with your coordinates. Found a dupe or exploit? Report it instead of using it: reporters get credit, not a ban.

topics.title: Staff
topics.answer: The server is run by **MrCoffeeBench** and the staff team. For anything that needs staff, use `/ticket <message>` in game or ask here. Staff will never ask for your password.

topics.title: Store or ranks
topics.answer: There's no store right now. Everything on the server is earned by playing.

topics.title: Quest book
topics.answer: There's no quest book in Season 3 at launch. Working through the advancement tree counts toward your level, so it's a guided path of its own. Any quest book would be announced here.

topics.title: VR
topics.answer: VR isn't part of the Season 3 pack. It was a Season 2 feature.

topics.title: Bedrock / mobile / console
topics.answer: The server is **Java Edition only**, and it needs the modpack (180+ mods), so you need a PC or Mac. Bedrock, consoles and phones can't join.

topics.title: Java version
topics.answer: Minecraft 1.21.1 runs on **Java 21**. Modrinth App, Prism and the CurseForge app install the right Java for you, so you normally don't have to do anything.

topics.title: What's in the pack
topics.answer: It's a Minecraft **1.21.1 NeoForge** pack with 180+ mods built around **Create** and **Create: Aeronautics** airships, plus Tectonic terrain, YUNG's structures, Numismatics, Distant Horizons, Simple Voice Chat and more. The full list is under **Mods** on the title screen.

topics.title: Wiki
topics.answer:
Everything's on the wiki: {wiki}
Start with *Getting Started*, then *Claims* before you build.

topics.title: Discord invite
topics.answer: Invite link: {discord}

topics.title: Changing your name
topics.answer: `/changename <newName>` changes your display name **once per account**, and staff approve it first. Premium players who change their Mojang name should contact staff.

topics.title: Clan tags
topics.answer: `/clan tag <tag>` puts a clan tag beside your name, `/clan color <color>` colours it and `/clan untag` removes it.

topics.title: Profiles and bios
topics.answer: `/profile` shows your profile and `/profile <player>` shows someone else's. Set your bio with `/setbio <text>`.

topics.title: The sidebar
topics.answer: The sidebar shows your level, Season 3 playtime and more. `/sidebar` turns it on or off for you.

topics.title: My corpse is gone
topics.answer: Your corpse stays where you died. Use `/back` (within 5 minutes of dying) to go straight there. If it's genuinely gone, open `/ticket <what happened and where>` and staff will look into it.
